Skelivka Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lviv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This record shares its community history with a separately documented cemetery named Nove Misto elsewhere in this collection, both apparently referring to the same underlying community, historically also known as Skelivka. Jews settled here in the early 17th century, becoming independent in the late 18th or early 19th century under Rabbi Aharon Itzhak (died 1860); the population peaked at 690 (51.9 percent of the village) around the turn of the 19th century. In the summer of 1942, most of the local Jewish population was expelled to the Bełżec death camp by way of the Sambir ghetto. This is the older of two separately catalogued 'Skelivka' cemeteries in this collection.
